## Task
Fix astropy issue #13579 (from TASK.md): `world_to_pixel` on a `SlicedLowLevelWCS` returns an erroneous result for one dimension when the 3D WCS has a PC matrix coupling spectral and spatial axes — while the full (unsliced) WCS is correct.

## Root cause
In `astropy/wcs/wcsapi/wrappers/sliced_wcs.py`, `SlicedLowLevelWCS.world_to_pixel_values` filled the **dropped** world dimensions with a hardcoded `1.` before delegating to the underlying WCS:

```python
else:
    world_arrays_new.append(1.)
```

When the PC matrix couples the sliced-out dimension (wavelength) to the kept ones (lon/lat), that arbitrary `1.` corrupts the inverse transform, so one spatial pixel coordinate comes out wrong.

## Fix (minimal, in source only — 1 file, +5/−1)
Compute the real world coordinates of the sliced-out dimensions by evaluating the full WCS at pixel 0 of the kept dimensions, and use those instead of `1.`:

```python
sliced_out_world_coords = self._pixel_to_world_values_all(
    *[0] * len(self._pixel_keep)
)
...
else:
    world_arrays_new.append(sliced_out_world_coords[iworld])
```
